papers.title: 'It's everybody's business': a multi-method study to co-develop and evaluate a web-based interprofessional Sexual Function Intimacy Concerns after Cancer educational programme (SexFICC) to upskill cancer healthcare providers.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: With improved survival rates, there is a growing population of cancer survivors who experience sexual health concerns following cancer treatment. These are widely recognised sequelae of cancer and cancer treatment, negatively impacting intimate relationships and quality of life. At least 40% (up to 100%) of people affected by cancer report concerns in this area. However, despite being well documented long-term challenges, they remain largely unaddressed by healthcare teams leading to further deterioration in sexual health. Healthcare providers identify this as an important quality of life issue; however, this does not translate into action. Barriers identified by healthcare providers include lack of knowledge, comfort and confidence, misconception of limited interventions and referral pathways available, and considerations regarding how to raise and discuss this topic. Coordinated systematic approaches for assessment and management of SFI concerns are lacking. The SexFICC Programme will address these gaps. SexFICC is an educational programme designed to improve sexual health outcomes in people affected by cancer by upskilling the cancer workforce in detecting and managing these issues throughout the cancer experience. No such training currently exists in the Australian context. METHODS AND ANALYSIS: A multi-phase mixed-methods design will be employed. Through co-design with key stakeholders (anticipated n=40), we will co-develop, user test (n=10 participants), evaluate (minimum n=50) and disseminate a clinically integrated education programme aimed at increasing knowledge, confidence and skills in addressing sexual health concerns with anticipated positive changes on practice. The programme will include an educational course and practical evidence-based resources for cancer healthcare providers and approaches to address sexual health unmet needs in all people affected by cancer, with a unique focus on identified priority populations. papers.title: Social relationships promote access to food and information in wild jackdaws.
papers.abstract: Many animals form differentiated social relationships that can influence fitness, but the mechanisms behind these benefits are often unclear. How does the presence of social partners during foraging enhance access to food or information? Might individuals also incur short-term costs, for example, by foregoing feeding opportunities to remain with and support social partners? Here, we investigated how social relationships shape foraging decisions and outcomes in wild jackdaws (Corvus monedula) using automated radio frequency identification (RFID) feeding stations where two birds could perch but only one could feed, with the other queueing behind ('dyadic events'). Bonded social partners (pair-bonded mates and kin) engaged in these dyadic events more frequently than other dyads and they coordinated their visits, as shown by shorter dyadic arrival latencies. Bonded partners also showed higher social tolerance and possibly social support, with feeding individuals benefitting from a lower probability of being displaced when a partner was present. Queuing individuals accepted short-term time costs to remain with their social partners. For juveniles, following their parents probably promoted access to social information about feeder use. These findings show that social relationships influence decision-making and foraging performance in the wild, revealing both benefits and costs of maintaining close bonds. Short-term effects on foraging success may therefore contribute to long-term fitness advantages of strong social relationships.

papers.title: A multigene phylogeny of Aphidiinae (Hymenoptera: Braconidae) supports a revised higher-level classification and reveals host-associated diversification.
papers.abstract: CONTEXT: The subfamily Aphidiinae (Hymenoptera: Braconidae) comprises specialised koinobiont endoparasitoids of aphids, many of which are widely used as biological control agents. However, higher-level relationships and taxonomic ranks within Aphidiinae remain contentious. AIMS: We aimed to reconstruct the higher-level phylogeny of Aphidiinae, reassess its tribal and subtribal classification using molecular and morphological evidence, and examine whether its evolutionary diversification was temporally associated with major ecological transitions in aphid lineages. TAXON: Aphidiinae Haliday, 1833 (Hymenoptera: Braconidae). METHODS: We reconstructed a multilocus phylogeny using three nuclear loci (28S D2, EF-1α, wingless) and four mitochondrial loci (COI, COII, Cytb, ND1) for 86 individuals (84 species, 22 genera). A partitioned concatenated matrix (3435 bp) was analysed using partitioned Bayesian inference and partitioned maximum likelihood. Divergence times were estimated using a fossil-calibrated Bayesian analysis, and diagnostic morphological characters were assessed in conjunction with the molecular results. KEY RESULTS: Major backbone relationships were largely congruent across methods. Ephedrini sensu lato was consistently recovered as paraphyletic because Toxares formed a deeply divergent and strongly supported lineage placed between Praini and Aphidiini. Combined molecular evidence and diagnostic morphology support the recognition of Toxarini trib. nov. as a distinct tribe. Within Aphidiini, two principal subclades were repeatedly recovered. The sampled representative of Monoctonina (Monoctonus), was recovered as sister to Trioxina. This placement, together with their shared elongate ovipositor sheath with the dorsal margin nearly straight to convex in the distal half, supports the provisional inclusion of Monoctonina within Trioxina pending broader generic sampling. Protaphidiina and Lysiphlebina were consistently recovered within the Aphidiina assembl

papers.title: In vivo functional analysis of Fatty-acyl desaturase 3 in sex pheromone biosynthesis and courtship behavior of Plutella xylostella.
papers.abstract: Moths rely on sex pheromones for long-distance mate attraction and recognition. The biosynthesis of moth sex pheromones involves multiple enzymatic steps, among which desaturases play a pivotal role in introducing carbon-chain unsaturation. However, the specific desaturases involved in sex pheromone biosynthesis in the diamondback moth, Plutella xylostella, remain largely unexplored. In this study, we identified a Δ11-desaturase gene, PxylDES3, from the pheromone gland transcriptome and generated a homozygous mutant line using the CRISPR/Cas9 system. Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) analysis revealed that the three major sex pheromone components (Z11-16:Ald, Z11-16:OH, and Z11-16:Ac) were significantly reduced, but not completely abolished, in homozygous mutant females compared with wild-type females. Behavioral assays demonstrated that the loss of PxylDES3 led to a significant reduction in female mating success, impaired male orientation preference, and attenuated male wing-fanning and hair-pencil responses. Notably, the residual pheromone components detected in mutant females suggest potential functional redundancy within the desaturase gene family. Collectively, these findings establish PxylDES3 as an important contributor to sex pheromone biosynthesis and courtship behavior in P. xylostella, and provide a potential target for pheromone-based pest management strategies.

papers.title: Dual-vacancy-engineered V2O3 with VOC covalent coupling enables ultrastable aqueous zinc-ion batteries at 10 A g-1.
papers.journal: Journal of colloid and interface science
papers.abstract: Achieving ultrafast kinetics and long-term durability in aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) remains challenging because the interplay between interfacial electronic structure and structural stability of vanadium oxide cathodes is poorly understood. Here, we design a locally graphitized carbon-encapsulated V2O3 cathode (V2O3@G-aC) featuring V/O dual vacancies and d-p-π conjugated vanadium‑oxygen‑carbon (VOC) interfaces, fabricated via flash Joule carbothermal reduction followed by terephthalic acid (TPA) mediated interfacial reconstruction and carbonization. Lewis acid-base interactions at the linker-metal node interface, coupled with pellet-confined carbonization, simultaneously introduce dual vacancies and covalent VOC bonding within a mesoporous graphitic shell. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that these engineered interfaces enable V → O → C charge delocalization by narrowing the V 3d-O 2p-C 2p band gaps, thereby accelerating Zn2+/H+ co-intercalation kinetics and suppressing vanadium dissolution. V2O3@G-aC delivers 346 mAh g-1 at 10 A g-1, which ranks among the highest for vanadium-based AZIBs cathodes, and retains 106 mAh g-1 after 20,000 cycles at 10 A g-1 with suppressed by-product accumulation. A flexible pouch cell retains 202 mAh g-1 after 200 cycles at 1 A g-1 and remains operational during a separate 180° bending demonstration. This work establishes d-p-π conjugated metal‑oxygen‑carbon interfaces as a design principle for stabilizing multivalent-ion cathodes under extreme cycling conditions.

papers.title: Refining AMOEBA Electrostatics for d-Glucose and 1→4-Linked d-Glucose Oligosaccharides.
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.abstract: Carbohydrate simulations are highly sensitive to the treatment of hydroxyl electrostatics because hydration, conformational sampling, and reactivity are governed by dense hydrogen-bonding networks. Here, we examine how oxygen quadrupole scaling affects AMOEBA d-glucose models generated with Poltype2 by comparing the standard 0.7 scaling with full 1.0 scaling for α- and β-d-glucose monosaccharides, 1→4-linked oligomers, and concentrated solutions. Increasing the oxygen quadrupole scaling from 0.7 to 1.0 improves monosaccharide hydration free energies, increases d-glucose-water hydrogen-bond counts and lifetimes, and strengthens hydroxyl electric-field projections without substantially altering hydration-shell structure. In 1→4-linked d-glucose oligomers, full scaling also enhances intramolecular hydrogen bonding, restricts conformational sampling, and produces more organized chain electrostatics. Electric-field decompositions indicate that OH2 and OH3 in α1→4 d-glucose oligomers are strongly coupled to intramolecular hydrogen-bond networks, whereas OH6 remains more water-controlled and solvent-accessible. Diffusion simulations show that both models perform reasonably well at concentrations up to 0.5 mol/kg but overestimate the slowdown of d-glucose mobility at higher concentrations, especially with 1.0 scaling. Overall, full oxygen quadrupole scaling improves local hydration, hydroxyl electrostatics, and diffusion behavior in the lower-concentration regime. Further refinement is needed to balance these stronger interactions against transport properties in highly concentrated carbohydrate solutions, which may be particularly relevant to materials applications.

papers.title: Dual Porphyrin Sensitized Photocatalytic System for Visible-Light-Driven CO2 Reduction.
papers.abstract: Dye-sensitized photocatalysis offers a powerful strategy for combining the molecular selectivity of transition-metal catalysts with the robustness and charge-separation capabilities of semiconductor materials. Herein, we report a dual porphyrin-sensitized TiO2 platform for visible-light-driven CO2 reduction, integrating a Zn-porphyrin photosensitizer with newly designed Fe-porphyrin catalysts bearing urea-based secondary-sphere functionalities. These hydrogen-bonding motifs promote CO2 preorganization and stabilization of key reduced intermediates at the metal center. Systematic comparison of homogeneous and heterogeneous systems reveals a pronounced enhancement in activity and durability upon immobilization onto TiO2 nanoparticles. Optimization studies demonstrate that catalytic activity is strongly governed by both sacrificial electron donor (SED) availability and proton concentration. Under anhydrous conditions, increased SED concentration boosts turnover numbers, while the introduction of controlled amounts of water enhances proton-coupled electron transfer but ultimately compromises catalyst stability at higher concentrations. Under optimized conditions, the best-performing assembly achieves turnover numbers (TONs) exceeding 15,000 after 96 h of irradiation, representing, to the best of our knowledge, the highest reported TON for Fe-porphyrin-based dye-sensitized photocatalytic systems (DSPs). These findings highlight the delicate balance between electron and proton management in dye-sensitized architectures and provide key design principles for developing durable and efficient molecular-semiconductor hybrids for solar-driven CO2 conversion.

papers.title: Strength in families: Parental resilience, marital dynamics, and adolescent anxiety and substance use.
papers.abstract: Drawing on Luthar's relational framework of resilience, this study examines how parental resilience operates within marital dynamics to shape adolescent adjustment in Mexican-origin families. Using four waves of data from 604 families (Madolage = 12.41, SD = 0.97; 54.3% girls), we tested a longitudinal cascade linking W1 parental resilience to W4 adolescent anxiety and substance use via W2 marital warmth, W3 marital satisfaction, and W3 adolescents' perceptions of interparental conflict. Actor-partner interdependence models revealed both intrapersonal and interpersonal pathways: wives' resilience predicted own marital warmth, whereas husbands' resilience predicted wives' warmth. Indirect effects indicated that wives' resilience was associated with lower adolescent anxiety and substance use through warmer marital interactions, higher marital satisfaction, and reduced perceived conflict. These findings position resilience as a promotive relational resource enacted within the marital dyad, advancing interparental positivity spillover theory by identifying parental resilience as upstream drivers of family processes that shape adolescent psychopathology.

papers.title: Beyond Legal Recognition: Parental Acceptance and Couple-Level Minority Stress on Same-Sex Couples' Well-Being in Chinese Societies.
papers.abstract: Previous studies in the Global North suggest that same-sex marriage brings positive impacts on the well-being of lesbian, gay, bisexual, queer, and plus (LGBQ+) individuals. Parental acceptance is challenging yet important for LGBQ+ individuals, especially in Chinese societies, which strongly emphasize harmony and heteronormative family relationships. This paper examines the association between the legal recognition of same-sex couple relationships and one's individual and relational well-being, and how it is mediated by parental acceptance and couple-level minority stress. We surveyed 812 LGBQ+ respondents in committed same-sex relationships in two Chinese-majority societies, Taiwan (with legal recognition of same-sex couple relationships) and Hong Kong (without such policy). We found that Taiwan respondents reported higher levels of parental acceptance and a lower level of couple-level stigma and discrimination than their counterparts in Hong Kong. While Taiwan respondents reported better relational well-being, there was no significant difference in individual well-being between the two societies. Experience of couple-level stigma and discrimination was associated with higher levels of depression. We argue that parental acceptance explains much of the significant variation in relationship satisfaction, beyond living in societies with or without legal recognition of same-sex couple relationships. As such, we underscore the importance of parental acceptance for LGBQ+ individuals in their relationship with their same-sex partners in Chinese societies. Furthermore, as same-sex couples continue to encounter couple-level minority stress and challenges in gaining parental acceptance, there is a need for mental health and social services to provide targeted support to enhance their well-being.

papers.title: The Role of Dyadic Coping in Relationship Satisfaction Among Couples Facing Cancer: A Meta-Analytic Actor-Partner Interdependence Approach.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the actor and partner effects of dyadic coping on relationship satisfaction and quality of life (QoL) in patients with cancer and their caregiving partners. METHODS: Four English-language and three Chinese-language databases were systematically searched for cross-sectional or longitudinal studies from inception to February 1, 2026. A meta-analytic Actor-Partner Interdependence Model using two-stage structural equation modeling was applied to synthesize correlation matrices and estimate actor and partner effects. WebMASEM was used to examine associations between dyadic coping and relationship satisfaction or QoL. RESULTS: Twelve studies comprising 2,859 cancer-affected dyads were included. All pooled correlations between dyadic coping and relationship satisfaction or QoL were statistically significant. Actor effects of dyadic coping on relationship satisfaction and QoL were significant for patients and caregiving partners. Among partner effects, the effect of caregiving partners' dyadic coping on patients' QoL was the only one to reach statistical significance. CONCLUSIONS: Dyadic coping demonstrated significant actor effects on relationship satisfaction and QoL for patients with cancer and caregiving partners. The effect of caregiving partners' dyadic coping on patients' QoL was the only partner effect to reach statistical significance. IMPLICATIONS FOR NURSING PRACTICE: These findings provide descriptive evidence indicating that dyadic coping in couples facing cancer is predominantly associated with an individual's own outcomes. Although consistent with the Systemic-Transactional Model, these cross-sectional associations do not support causal inferences regarding intervention mechanisms. Longitudinal dyadic designs are required to evaluate whether these association patterns persist over time and to test moderators including cancer stage, cultural context, and caregiver burden.

papers.title: "After radiation sessions, I sometimes feel weak and dizzy'': Experiences of Ghanaian women with breast cancer post radiotherapy.
papers.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Breast cancer remains one of the main causes of morbidity and mortality among females worldwide. Despite the advancement of several treatment options such as surgery, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy to tackle this disease, several women still refuse these allopathic treatment options due to adverse effects posed by these treatment modalities which usually remain poorly identified and managed particularly in low-resourced-constrained settings like those in Sub-Saharan Africa. AIM: We explored the experiences of Ghanaian women with breast cancer being nursed after undergoing radiotherapy. METHOD: This was an exploratory descriptive qualitative study involving seventeen (17) women diagnosed with breast cancer who had undergone radiotherapy at a Teaching Hospital in Kumasi, Ghana. The participants were engaged in in-depth interviews using a piloted interview guide. The interviews were audio-taped, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using thematic analysis with the help of Nvivo 10. RESULTS: Two main themes emerged from this study; physical experiences and social experiences. The sub-themes under the physical experiences included pain, breast and skin changes, physical exhaustion, and gastrointestinal symptoms. Regarding social experiences, we identified three sub-themes, mainly, family and partner support, support from employers, churches, and friends, and finally sexual life challenges. CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATION: Several physical experiences post radiation therapy deter women diagnosed with breast cancer from consenting to undergo radiotherapy or recommending radiotherapy as a treatment option for breast cancer in Ghana. However, the social networks of women with breast cancer undergoing radiation therapy could serve as useful motivators in promoting radiation therapy. papers.title: Criminal dismemberments: Victim, suspect, and incident attributes of decapitation-only and dismemberment homicides.
papers.abstract: Using cases of criminal dismemberment in the CDC's National Violent Death Reporting System (NVDRS), we directly compared decapitation-only and dismemberment homicides. We also explored clusters of victim, suspect, and incident variables, including how decapitation-only and dismemberment homicides fit within the clusters. Victims who were only decapitated were more likely to be recovered in a residence and were more likely to be the suspect's child or other relative. Additionally, decapitated-only victims were more likely to be a juvenile. Victims of decapitation-only homicides were more likely to be linked to a suspect who was on scene when first responders arrived or was in acute mental health crisis compared with homicides in which the victims were dismembered. Dismemberment homicides were more likely to involve multiple suspects, movement of the body from the homicide location, or concealment of the body (burial, wrapping/placement of the body into a container). Adult victims under the age of 65 were more likely to be dismembered. The cluster analysis yielded results consistent with the direct comparison and identified a third cluster of incidents involving intimate partner violence between current/former romantic partners. Our findings highlight the utilitarian nature of most criminal dismemberments and counter stereotypes of offenders who target strangers or dismember while experiencing mental illness.

papers.title: Assessing formal service providers' readiness to address IPV among women with disabilities in Sweden: A mixed-methods analysis.
papers.abstract: Women with disabilities face a heightened risk of intimate partner violence (IPV), yet formal support systems often remain ill-equipped to address their specific needs. This study assesses indicators of readiness among formal service providers in Sweden, including healthcare, social services, shelters, the police, and the Centre against Violence, to support women with disabilities who experience IPV. Employing a sequential exploratory mixed-methods design, the study combined qualitative interviews (N = 18) with a national survey (N = 1,151). Data analysis was guided by an adapted version of Colombini et al.'s readiness framework, focusing on structural, organizational, and provider-level dimensions. The findings indicate that, at the structural level, reported facilitators of readiness include functional collaborative spaces, coordination, and knowledge-sharing mechanisms. However, fragmented inter-institutional collaboration and limited resources emerged as key barriers to the structural conditions required to optimally support women with disabilities subjected to IPV. At the organizational level, readiness was hindered by the absence of disability-inclusive IPV guidelines and persistent accessibility barriers, such as physical, information, and communication inaccessibility. At the provider level, many service providers expressed a need for more training on disability-specific issues, often relying instead upon personal experience or peer support when handling IPV cases. Nonetheless, supportive workplace environments and collegial networks were identified as key enablers of emotional resilience and professional learning. The findings of this study underscore the need for inclusive policies, comprehensive targeted training, and inter-sectoral collaboration to enhance the readiness of IPV support systems for women with disabilities.
